text:
A Django **project** is the overall container for your site – it is the Django installation together with a set of configuration files (the settings module, URLs, WSGI, etc.) that tell Django how the whole site should behave [1]. Think of the project as the “website” itself; it holds the global configuration and can contain many separate pieces of functionality.

An **app** is one of those pieces. It is a self‑contained bundle of code that provides a specific feature: models, views, templates, and URL patterns that work together to implement something like a blog, a forum, or a payment system [1]. Because an app is independent of the surrounding project, you can drop the same app into different projects and reuse it [1].

So the key distinction is scope: the project defines the whole Django environment and its settings, while an app is a modular, reusable component that lives inside a project and delivers a particular set of functionality [1].
